## Why This Is Asked
Tests precise bitfield extraction in arbitrary alignments, a common requirement in parsers and low-level codecs. No loops or branches; relies on safe shifts and masks.

- Dynamic masking with shifts
- Handling width up to 64 without UB
- LSB 0 indexing, endianness-agnostic interpretation

## Code Example
```javascript
uint64_t extractBits(uint64_t word, int start, int width) {
  return (word >> start) & ((~0ULL) >> (64 - width));
}
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you adapt for start and width as signed inputs?  
- How to validate input without affecting performance?

## Why This Is Asked
This question evaluates fundamental understanding of bitwise operations and rotation algorithms without using control flow, testing core computer architecture knowledge and low-level programming skills.

## Key Concepts
- Bitwise shifts and their behavior with overflow
- Bit masking for input validation and range constraints
- Rotation invariants and proper edge case handling
- Branch-free optimization techniques
- Understanding of two's complement arithmetic at the bit level

## Code Example
```c
// rotateLeft32 implementation with no loops or conditionals
uint32_t rotateLeft32(uint32_t x, unsigned int r) {
    r &= 31;  // Mask to valid range
    return (x << r) | (x >> (32 - r));
}
```

## Interview Context
This problem tests candidates' ability to think at the bit level and implement efficient, branch-free code—skills essential for systems programming, embedded development, and performance-critical applications.

This tests precise bit manipulations without branches, a common need in codecs and bitboards.

- Bitwise shifts and masks

- Handling 0-31 safely without undefined behavior

uint32_t rotateLeft32(uint32_t x, unsigned k){

}
